title: Civilian-protection combat layer
summary: Combat maps get seeded with civilian concentrations, large vehicles, and infrastructure (all with statblocks) as enemy-attackable targets; a medic can heal them with an outsized effect (originally the ground-role students, cut 2026-09-20); an end-of-combat HP-vs-max report scores how well the city was protected.
description:
Originally written for the ground-level civil-defense layer (the ground roles, cut 2026-09-20): seed combat maps with civilian concentrations, vehicles (trains, planes, ships, anything large), and key infrastructure/buildings — all given statblocks. Enemies get to attack these directly (buildings, infrastructure, the civilian population) as valid targets, not just the PCs/Frames. Medics (as captured, non-piloting students; that role went with the ground roles, and who takes it now is open) could perform heal actions against these targets with a much larger effect than normal healing math would give, specifically undoing the damage enemy attacks cause to civilians. At the end of a combat, compare the HP of all surviving friendly units (civilian/vehicle/infrastructure included) against their max HP, and generate a report on the encounter from that comparison — a scorable 'how well did you protect the city' outcome, distinct from simple win/lose.

This is a mechanization of the 'defensible assets' idea already noted in design/campaign-arc.md's evolving-mechanics-threads section (world map / satellite-scale combat with assets to defend) — this idea is the concrete combat-mechanic version of that.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump.
openSubQuestions: Exact statblock shape for civilian/vehicle/infrastructure targets — how detailed, and does creature.schema.json/combatStatblock fit or does this need its own lighter shape?
How much bigger 'outsized' healing-on-civilians should be — a flat multiplier? A different heal-action entirely for medics?
What the end-of-combat report actually contains and where/how it gets generated and shown to the table.
